That is the honest reading: a strict ladder would mark whichever I happened to write first and be wrong two thirds of the time. notes: THE BRANCH IS THE MISSION. Bullet 3 says outright that the rest can be done two ways -- Bastok then Windurst, or Windurst then Bastok -- and the four After-sections show they are not the same walkthrough with the order swapped: the BCNM belongs to whichever nation you visit SECOND (Balga's Dais against Searcher and Black Dragon if Windurst is second, Waughroon Shrine against Seeker and Dark Dragon if Bastok is second), and even Kupipi's key item differs (Dark key on the Bastok-first route, Shield offering on the Windurst-first route). None of that expresses as one ordered ladder, and inventing a merged path would send half of all players to a fight they do not have to do -- worse than no rung at all. So only the SPINE is modelled: Halver sends you out; the two San d'Orian Consulates -- Savae E Paleade in the Metalworks and Mourices in Windurst Woods -- are an unordered pair, because each nation's leg both opens and closes on its consulate whichever order you pick; then Halver again. The [KI] Kindred report sits on the last member of the pair for the same reason as the sword in 2-1: it is granted by whichever consulate you visit second, so holding it is precisely the moment the mark should leave the pair and land on Halver, and that is true on both routes. The item legs (a Mine Gravel refined to Mythril Sand at Palborough Mines; two Parana Shields from Zhuu Buxu the Silent) are branch-specific and are not modelled. The Reward's [KI] Adventurer's Certificate is a reward and never evidence. Start stays the generic Gate Guard from the header, kept as Ambrotien in agreement with chronicle, even though the walkthrough opens on Halver -- the mission is accepted from a guard and the ladder starts where the page starts.

notes:
START MOVED, AND SAID SO. chronicle's giver for this row is the string "san d'orian embassy in ru'lude gardens" and the header's Start says the same thing -- a PLACE, not an NPC. The shipped index draws it as npc key 'san d'orian embassy in ru'lude gardens' in zone 243, a key no live entity can ever match, which is the Carbuncle Debacle case exactly. The walkthrough names the actual entities in its first bullet: you speak with Nelcabrit and then click Door: San d'Orian Emb. So start.npc is NELCABRIT, a real NPC that resolves, and the header string is kept verbatim in start.raw. That is a marker move from a key that matches nothing to one that matches somebody, not a removal -- but it IS a move, and the builder makes it silently, so it is flagged and stated here.

THE THREE MAGICITE. Bullet 4 is one line, 'Obtain the 3 Magicite Key Items', expanded in three After-sections; they may be done in any order, so they are one group of three and all draw at once. All three key items sit as an AND-list on the LAST member because the mission needs all three and an item may be evidence only once: holding Optistone, Orastone and Aurastone together is exactly when the mark should leave the group for the Audience Chamber. The Oztroja and Beadeaux runs carry their prerequisite key items in `items` -- the [KI] Yagudo torch (Paya-Sabya then Muckvix; the page says the cutscene will not fire without it even if somebody else opens the way) and the [KI] Coruscant rosary and Black matinee necklace that open the Qulun Dome door. Those two come from Mysteries of Beadeaux I and II, which are SEPARATE QUESTS, so their trades are not rungs of this mission.

THE SILVER BELL IS NOT EVIDENCE. Bullet 3 says a player who did this mission for another nation already holds it and still needs the cutscene, so holding it would prove nothing about this step. Left out deliberately. The Airship Pass and the 10,000 gil are Rewards, and [KI] Message to Jeuno (San d'Oria) does not resolve against res/key_items.lua at all -- none of the three is evidence.
